questions.title: "What level of judicial review applies when evaluating an executive order based on Congress's authority in §1182(f)?"
questions.question_body:
"I read Pacito where judges cite Trump v HAWAII calling "deference" attached to Section 1182(f).  Does that mean they apply strict scrutiny, rational‑basis scrutiny, or some other standard when reviewing a President’s blanket suspension of refugees?

As I understand it courts normally defer heavily in immigration matters; however here they said the President has already met his mandate so it's about likelihood success.

How should I think about what review level really applies during such challenges, especially when a statute says buyers rarely face criminality’??"

questions.title: "Is Congress imposing mandatory refugee resettlement standards through §1522(a)(1)(A), or merely giving the Secretary permission?"
questions.question_body:
"In Pacito Judge Lee argues that sections copyrighted ’Authorization’ indicate discretion while subsection (a)(1)(A)’s word "shall" simply starts a conditional requirement triggered only if appropriate funds exist.

That feels contradictory—a bill written ’shall provision,’ yet arguments say agency discretion determines whether programs get funded.

How do courts decide whether wording implies obligation versus permissibility?

What tests assess whether Congress intended us obligation even when resources are limited?

And does such analysis affect litigation over cuts made against USRAP financing?
"

questions.title: "Do NGOs lose standing when Fed grants supporting USRAP collaborative agreements are terminated via an Executive Order?"
questions.question_body:
"Three nonprofits sued after Exec Order No 14169 defunded USRAP and pulled its cooperative agreements.

Are they entitled to sue merely because their contracts were abruptly ended?

Does contract law recognize termination upon emergency policy changes—butpun unexpected order—as possibly actionable?

Have courts ever granted rescission‑type relief against a federal agency solely based on expedited termination tied explicitly to presidential policy?
"

questions.title: "Difference between administrative stays issued by courts versus stays issued by administrative agencies."
questions.question_body:
"The opinion refers repeatedly to our own stay denounced June 17**a'am When ognaative indeed revoked July 18 admin temptation sup swapped speculation! 

I see references to "administrative stay" promulgated July 18 and later cancelled.

What separates those from judicial stays?

Who holds authority over reversing them?

If a court cancels its own adjournment‑style order against another—how’s that different procedurally?
"

questions.title: "When can federal agencies be forced under APA rules to fund refugee reception programs despite lack‑of‐appropriation constraints?"
questions.question_body:
"Pacito holds some claims fail under APA partly because Congress only mandated service provision conditional upon available appropriations.

Could plaintiffs succeed even though FY2025 cuts reduced funding drastically? \u0020\u0020Cite precedent where courts compelled government beyond its approved budget.

Essentially—is exhaustion‑of‑appropriations shielding agencies from civil liability against “failure‑to‑provide” claims?
"

questions.title: "How do congressional appropriations interact with statutes titled “Authorization” such as §§152|2250 regarding refugee assistance?"
